allowed_dependency_manifest.content: For each integer n at least 2, among all length n minus 1 sequences of plus or minus 1, determine exactly which sign patterns maximize the number of permutations of 1 through n whose consecutive differences have the prescribed signs.

forbidden_claims.statement_nl: Let $n$ be an integer with $n \\geq 2$. For a sequence $s = (s_1,\\dots,s_{n-1})$ where each $s_i = \\pm 1$, let $f(s)$ be the number of permutations $(a_1,\\dots,a_n)$ of $\\{1,2,\\dots,n\\}$ such that $s_i(a_{i+1}-a_i) > 0$ for all $i$. For each $n$, determine the sequences $s$ for which $f(s)$ is maximal.

statement_nl: Let n be an integer at least 2, let s=(s_1,...,s_{n-1}) with each s_i in {+1,-1}, and for each k with 1 <= k <= n define a vector v^(k)=(v^(k)_1,...,v^(k)_k) by declaring v^(k)_j to be the number of permutations b=(b_1,...,b_k) of {1,...,k} such that s_i(b_{i+1}-b_i)>0 for every 1 <= i < k and b_k is the j-th smallest element of {b_1,...,b_k}. Then v^(1)=(1). Moreover, for each k with 1 <= k <= n-1 and each j with 1 <= j <= k+1, with empty sums interpreted as 0, if s_k=+1 then v^(k+1)_j = sum_{i=1}^{j-1} v^(k)_i, while if s_k=-1 then v^(k+1)_j = sum_{i=j}^{k} v^(k)_i. In particular, if f(s) denotes the number of permutations a=(a_1,...,a_n) of {1,...,n} with s_i(a_{i+1}-a_i)>0 for all 1 <= i <= n-1, then f(s)=sum_{j=1}^n v^(n)_j.
